newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ, News lift Australian stocks to record close.
newsitem.headline: ANZ, News lift Australian stocks to record close.

text.p: The Australian share market posted a record closing high on Thursday, buyers encouraged by good news from Rupert Murdoch's News Corp and takeover rumours for Australia and New Zealand Banking Group.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 24.4 points higher at 2,638.1, 9.2 points above Tuesday's record mark. The index also set a new record intra-day high at 2,646.4.
The June share price index settled 25 points firmer at 2,653 and at a 14.9 point premium to the underlying index.
News Corp was favoured throughout the session after it pleased investors by offloading its U.S. satellite TV assets.
The media group also said it would pay US$1.9 billion for for children's cable TV network, International Family Entertainment.

"These deals will be a very big positive for News, firstly because they haven't used DPs (preferred shares) and they've conserved their cash," said Vince Pepe, media analyst at brokerage ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
News ordinary shares ended 40 cents higher at A$6.27 (US$4.70) and News preferred stock closed 42 cents up at A$5.23.
ANZ shares were more volatile, jumping 78 cents to a record high of A$10.00 early, but ending up 56.2 cents at A$9.782.

Old rumours that a foreign bank would soon announce a bid for ANZ sent the bank's shares racing. But profit-taking and an announcement from the bank saying it was unaware of any reason for the rise in its share price cut the rise in half by lunch.
Dealers said the rumour persisted into afternoon trade and could continue to move the stock on Friday.

"Market direction is always dependent on what happens on Wall Street but so long as it (Wall Street) doesn't fall out of bed, I would be looking for another strong day tomorrow with News Corp continuing to improve and ANZ maybe going for another run," a Brisbane-based dealer said.
The resource sector trailed industrials on the day despite a strong performance from Rio Tinto which rose 46 cents to A$21.98 after talk of analysts upgrades out of London.
Bellwether issue Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd closed slightly firmer but on relatively light volume, investors engrossed by the action in the bank and media sectors.
Nickel and gold producer and explorer Highlands Pacific made a steady debut, its stock opening at its issue price of A$1.00 and closing at A$1.02 on volume of 3.6 million shares.
